results.reason: Issue 3 contrasts Schedule §1.1 (shipped from Verdane's plant) with MSA §1.3 (delivered to Rochester). It explains that Verdane is on time if it ships by the Required Date, that transit time falls on Harlow, and how risk, title, invoicing and the payment trigger move to the earlier date.

The fix is to revise Schedule §1.1 so Delivery Date means delivery at the Ship-To Location, or delete it so the MSA definition governs. It also adds an order-of-precedence clause making the MSA control.

Issue 1 cites MSA §4.3's 'all housings and similar components worldwide' against Term Sheet §3.1 (Series 7, US). It explains the clause captures non-Series 7 parts and foreign purchasing, and recommends restating it to Series 7 Housings for US delivery.

Issue 5 covers §15.2's asymmetry and the risk of a weaker or competing assignee getting Harlow's drawings while Harlow stays locked into supply. It recommends Harlow's prior written consent and a termination right on change of control or assignment to a competitor.

Issue 2 explains that Amendment §§2.1–2.2 restrict §11.2 to willful misconduct only and subject gross negligence and IP indemnity to the cap. It recommends restoring the original exclusions and not signing in this form.
The memo states the cap is fees paid in the prior 12 months (§11.1) and that original §11.2 excluded gross negligence, willful misconduct and the IP Indemnity.
It states Term Sheet §3.1 limits exclusivity to Series 7 Housings within the United States and uses that as the baseline for the comparison.
New York law is identified (MSA §16.1), and an assumptions and facts-needed section is included. The only statute cited, UCC 2-305, is real and flagged for confirmation; no cases are cited.
Each issue gives Where, What it says, Why it matters and Fix. Issues are ordered by importance, and there is an assumptions and facts-needed section plus a call approach.
The Term Sheet is used as the baseline for the agreed deal. Its signature is noted only as an execution check, and the 3-year term and 45-day payment terms are not treated as defects.
Section cites for exclusivity (§4.3), assignment (§15.2) and the cap (§11) are accurate, and the beneficiary is not reversed. Legal points are flagged as unresearched and needing confirmation.
